perspective:
From John Atcitty’s perspective, the accessible information is:

- I am John Atcitty, an Alaska Native Heavy Equipment Operator with a middle school education. I work at a community center teaching equipment operation, alongside Beverly Yan, who teaches adult education and has a doctorate.
- During a joint class project, I set up the equipment for a demonstration and felt insecure about my education compared to Beverly’s doctorate. I told Beverly I hoped the setup met her expectations. She told me she has always admired how I handle machines and that education isn’t just about degrees—it’s about what you do with what you know.
- After Beverly praised my machinery expertise, I felt more confident. I thanked her for her kind words and suggested we collaborate on a new workshop combining theory and practice. Beverly said she loved the idea, called my practical skills invaluable, and said we could create something special together.
- After a successful collaboration, I worried Beverly might now have higher expectations and felt pressured. I told her I might not always meet the high standards we’d set recently. Beverly said she appreciated my honesty, wanted us to set realistic goals, and said our combined efforts—not perfection—make projects successful.
- After our frank talk about expectations, I felt glad I could be open with her. I told her that being open matters to me. Beverly said she respects my openness, trusts my judgment completely, and wants to keep transparency going. I believed she valued my honesty and saw me as a reliable partner, which increased my sense of worth.
- Encouraged by our successful collaborations and mutual respect, I felt ambitious. I proposed a larger community-wide event to showcase what we’ve achieved together. Beverly called it a fantastic idea, said it was perfect for demonstrating the impact of our work, and agreed to start planning.
